newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-BP shares fall as Kuwait sells 3 pct.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-BP shares fall as Kuwait sells 3 pct.

text.p: Shares in British Petroleum Co Plc fell sharply on Thursday following overnight news the Kuwait Investment Office (KIO) was selling a three percent stake in the oil giant.

The deal, worth about 1.25 billion pounds ($2.1 billion) and one of the largest block sales ever on the London Stock Exchange, is a "rebalancing" exercise, said KIO which will continue to hold 6.3 percent of BP.
Dealers, meanwhile, noted that most of the shares put up for sale were already placed overnight with mainly U.S. investors.
Investment bank Goldman Sachs, which handles the deal, said there was substantial demand from institutional and private investors across the globe.
The bank delined to say whether the sale had already been completed by late morning when BP was down 18 pence at 726-1/2.
The stocks have been among the best performing world oil shares in recent years as the company embarked on a massive cost-cutting programme in the early 1990s.
The efficiency drive was carried out after BP slashed its dividend in 1992 when the company was suffering from a heavy debt burden.
The KIO built up its holding in BP when a sale of BP stock by the British government coincided with the 1987 stock market crash. BP later bought back part of the holding from the KIO.

The investment group said "the holding of of British Petroleum shares has...come to represent a disproportinate part of the Future Generation Fund of Kuwait and this is why this rebalancing exercise is now being undertaken."
The Future Generation Fund of Kuwait is managed by the KIO.
Industry analysts were unperturbed by the stake sale, saying it would not have an impact on the company's operations, and they expected the shares to recover quickly.
"The fact somebody sells shares does not change the fundamentals of the company," said Paul Spedding at Kleinwort Benson. ($ = 0.608 British Pounds)
